solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Search to capture alien life? It's an obsession

indicators.note: the search word holds the alien inside it, as a net captures a catch

parts.note: to fish for something is to search for it
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial, stands for alien life

explanation.surface: A quest for extraterrestrial beings is mocked as someone's obsessive hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is a fixation, something a person is irrationally devoted to, so it is a synonym for obsession.

clue.text: Feeble books covered by attack

indicators.note: covered by means the books sit inside the attack word

parts.note: to flay is to attack severely, literally or with words
B is an abbreviation for book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: A weak set of books is torn apart by a critic's attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby means slack and lacking firmness, hence weak or feeble.

clue.text: One that's cuddled is naked, we hear, underneath some lingerie

indicators.note: underneath places the sound-alike piece below the lingerie piece in this down entry

parts.note: a teddy is a one-piece undergarment

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: bare means naked

explanation.surface: Someone is naked except for a little underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is a soft toy that children hug and cuddle.

clue.text: A lot of criticism about old philosopher

indicators.note: about means going round, so the trimmed criticism word wraps the letter for old
a lot of means most of, so the criticism word loses its last letter

parts.note: stick is informal British for criticism, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker took a great deal of criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic is a follower of Zeno's ancient school, which taught enduring hardship calmly, so a philosopher.

clue.text: Left-wing material: it starts to parody Reagan (amongst America's foremost Republicans)

indicators.note: foremost asks for the leading letter of the word America's
amongst places the following group of letters among those of the Republican party abbreviation

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A satirist's piece lampooning Reagan is dismissed by his supporters as leftist propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: Reagan's name tempts a solver toward the right wing, but the Republicans here only supply their Grand Old Party initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitprop is political propaganda, historically from Soviet agitation and propaganda bodies, hence material from the left.

clue.text: Dark hours, fight with adversary going badly

indicators.note: going badly suggests things in disarray, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A battle against an enemy is turning out poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: The graveyard shift is the overnight work period, the dark hours between midnight and morning.

clue.text: Drunk leading group of climbers where falling is always likely?

indicators.note: leading puts the drunk word in front of the climbers word

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a rope is a team of mountaineers roped together

explanation.surface: A drunk heading up a climbing party is bound to fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope walker balances on a thin taut wire, a place where a slip and fall is ever-present.

clue.text: Most of bar cheers, Indian dish being provided

indicators.note: most of means the bar word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rail is a bar
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: At a pub bar, toasts are raised while Indian food is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a cool yogurt side dish from Indian cuisine, often served with curry.

clue.text: Material for cast includes Pinter's second column

indicators.note: includes means the casting material holds the next letter within it

parts.note: plaster of Paris is the material used to set a broken limb in a cast

indicators.note: second asks for the second letter of the playwright's name

explanation.surface: A theatre cast's materials include something from a Pinter play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' suggests actors in Pinter's play, but here it is a plaster cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a rectangular column projecting slightly from a wall, so a kind of column.

clue.text: Excellent European breeding ground: limited measure going out the window

parts.note: def is slang for excellent
a nest is where birds breed
a ration is a fixed, limited allowance

explanation.surface: A splendid European habitat suffers under restricted measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenestration is throwing someone out of a window, as in the Defenestrations of Prague.

clue.text: Adaptation of drama done for stars

indicators.note: an adaptation reworks a piece, so these letters are rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A stage play has been adapted to suit its celebrity cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' reads as the actors of the adaptation, but it defines a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation of the northern sky, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Old King taking on difficult question

indicators.note: taking on means the king's letters take on more letters after them

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
ill can mean difficult or hard, as in ill at ease or ill-tempered times

explanation.surface: An ageing monarch faces a tough question from his court.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to interrogate them closely, so it is a verb sense of question.

clue.text: No room for Crazy Horse

indicators.note: no here means going without, so the room abbreviation is removed from the word for crazy

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: There is no space for the famous Sioux chief Crazy Horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy Horse' reads as the Lakota leader; split it, with 'Crazy' as BARMY and 'Horse' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a reddish-brown horse with black mane and tail, so it is an example of a horse.

clue.text: Isn't cleared after waving ID?

indicators.note: waving means the letters are shaken about and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flashing an identity card at a checkpoint still isn't let through.
explanation.definitionFit: Credentials are documents proving identity, which is what ID stands for: identification papers.

clue.text: Satisfied with story overlooking a display of courage

parts.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it, so met means satisfied

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the story word leaves out the clue's 'a'

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A storyteller is pleased with a tale of bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Mettle is spirit and resilience in the face of difficulty, shown when someone acts bravely.

clue.text: Bill and Grant touring the French plateau

indicators.note: touring means going around, so bill and grant together enclose the French article

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
to land someone something is to give or grant it, as in landing a prize
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Two men, Bill and Grant, are on a tour of a French upland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill and Grant' look like two travellers' names; they are TAB and LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableland is a broad, raised flat region, which is the same thing as a plateau.

clue.text: One that's fostered trouble with power and support

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
P is the physics symbol for power
a tee supports a golf ball before it is struck

explanation.surface: A foster child brings trouble along with energy and needs support.
explanation.definitionFit: An adoptee is a person taken into a family and raised there, much as a fostered child is.

clue.text: Play sadly no Electra

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A theatre regrets that Sophocles's tragedy is not being staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a stage drama such as Electra, but it is the slack in a mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the permitted variation or looseness in engineering parts, also called play.

clue.text: Unusual male singing voice framed in female singing voice

indicators.note: in means the framed word sits within the voice word

parts.note: alto is a lower female or high male singing voice
a picture is set in a frame, so set means framed

explanation.surface: An odd high-pitched male voice is set within a female voice part.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high register a man uses to sing above his normal range.

clue.text: Performer about to hold up a performer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the second performer goes round the rest

parts.note: an act is a performer or troupe on a variety bill
to hold up a bank is to rob it

explanation.surface: One entertainer is about to stage a robbery on another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' sounds theatrical (an acrobat holding up a partner) but means rob.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a gymnastic entertainer, one type of performer in a circus.

clue.text: Letter spelled out work in detail

parts.note: dee is the name of the letter D written as a word
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Someone spelling out a letter works through it in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something deeply is to study it thoroughly, examining it in detail.

clue.text: A stag I bagged in French location

indicators.note: bagged means captured, so the stag word holds the letter I

parts.note: a stag party is men only, so stag means men's

explanation.surface: A hunter shot a stag in rural France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stag' looks like a deer hunted and bagged, but it means men's, as in a stag night.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a city in northern France, capital of the Somme department.

clue.text: Made to look old, nothing modern getting stored round about

indicators.note: round about means the storage word wraps itself around the other pieces

parts.note: stashed means stored away or hidden
O, the round zero, means nothing
new means modern

explanation.surface: New goods are artificially aged while being stored.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewashed jeans are tumbled with stones to fade them, giving new denim a worn, aged appearance.

clue.text: University pleasant after eliminating one measure

parts.note: OU is the Open University

indicators.note: after eliminating means the pleasant word with the following letter removed

parts.note: nice means pleasant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A university finds a pleasant way to drop a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound, so a measure.

clue.text: Discourage day trip after Juliet drops out

indicators.note: drops out means the Juliet letter leaves the trip word

parts.note: a jaunt is a short pleasure trip
Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An outing is put off after Juliet withdraws from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juliet' hints at Shakespeare, but it is the radio code word for J.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt is to intimidate or dishearten, which makes it a synonym for discourage.

clue.text: Booze in unconfirmed story not for us

indicators.note: not for means the word for 'belonging to us' is left out of the story

parts.note: a rumour is an unconfirmed story
our is the possessive belonging to us

explanation.surface: A rumour of drink going round is not meant for our ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane, so it is a type of booze, an informal word for alcohol.

clue.text: After setback, Aleutians' leader appreciated capturing Northern islands

indicators.note: after a setback means the whole assembly is turned back to front
leader asks for the opening letter of the Aleutian word
capturing means the appreciated word encloses the northern letter

parts.note: to get something is to understand or appreciate it, so got

explanation.surface: An Aleutian chief welcomes the capture of some Arctic islands after a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After setback' reverses A + GNOT to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific nation made up of over a hundred and seventy islands.

clue.text: Impact of popular complaint in French church

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
flu is an illness, a complaint
en is the French word for in
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A common illness spreading within a French church has an effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Influence and impact both mean the effect one thing has upon another.

clue.text: Excessive start to opera: composer's last in different form?

indicators.note: start to asks for the opening letter of the word opera
the composer's final letter, a Roman numeral, is rewritten as the same number in words

parts.note: Verdi is the Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: Critics complain that an opera's composer overworked his final piece in another version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last in different form' turns Verdi's last letter I, the Roman one, into ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone means overstated or taken too far, so it describes something excessive.

clue.text: Description of heart of classy city

indicators.note: the description is of the central pair, so it is set between those two letters, saying which comes first
heart of asks for the middle letters of the word classy

parts.note: describing a pair of letters in order means saying one and then the other, so the description supplies then

explanation.surface: A tourist blurb describing the elegant centre of a fine city.
explanation.walkthrough: Describe the heart of 'classy' (AS) in words, A then S, and the description itself spells the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece, a famous ancient city.
